summary: Four inactive proofs reconstruct global decreasing smooth strictly admissible approximation of every bounded Hermitian Hessian potential in its standard upper-test/subharmonic representative. A penalty squeeze works for upper semicontinuous potentials without a nonlinear product. It identifies continuous envelopes of smooth obstacles with the envelope over bounded competitors. Smooth decreasing majorants and geometrically decreasing uniform errors then produce uniformly bounded, strictly admissible decreasing approximants. This supplies an approximation input, not monotone convergence of bounded nonlinear products or bounded domination/regularity.
mathematical_checks: Compactness and upper semicontinuity give an actual maximum against each smooth penalized potential.
The (1+1/N) upper test and polarized Garding inequality give d_N >= (N+1)^(-m), independent of a product of the bounded potential.
The penalty error depends only on the fixed obstacle and b; it tends to zero before changing the obstacle.
The continuous obstacle envelope dominates every bounded upper-test competitor by that same squeeze.
Sup-distance regularization yields decreasing continuous majorants; errors of size 4^(-j)/4 preserve strict decrease after smoothing.
The continuous envelopes decrease to the bounded potential; adding the geometric error to smooth admissible approximants preserves both strict admissibility and monotonicity.
The point-spike example distinguishes the standard canonical representative from an arbitrary upper semicontinuous representative of a distribution.
The local KN26 comparison is unshifted dd^c u; it does not justify a shifted nonclosed global comparison by notation replacement.
primary_boundary: The fresh reads inspect exact definitions and selected approximation/comparison arguments. They are not complete new primary-paper reads. The declared classical linear equivalence has not been independently reconstructed in full.

selected_candidates.title: Dolbeault Cohomology Growth under Curvature Rank Bounds
selected_candidates.abstract: Let $L$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$, and let $r$ be the maximal rank of its curvature. We prove that $h^q(X,L^p\otimes E)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed holomorphic vector bundle $E$, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every degree $q$. No positivity, constant-rank, or K\"ahler assumption is imposed. Consequently, the Kodaira--Iitaka dimension satisfies $\kappa(L|_{X_0})\le r$ on every connected component $X_0$ of $X$. The proof retains rank identities in finite Taylor jets under successive rescalings and factors bounded Hermitian kernels without a positive lower bound on the absolute values of the nonzero curvature eigenvalues. Exact Dolbeault restriction identities yield finite-rank approximations with additive rank bounds, which control cohomology.

selected_candidates.title: Combs and complex structures on the six-sphere
selected_candidates.abstract: We construct complex structures on the six-sphere $S^6$ with arbitrarily large local Kuranishi dimension. As a corollary, we find the same phenomenon holds for the smooth manifold underlying complex projective 3-space $\mathbb{P}^3$.
